description:
Proposal: ../interp-proposal.html (One Plan Fact). Measured 2026-09-14 on main f26264572.

One question, "which inputs does this plan read, and how deeply", is answered by four walks at four moments over two node sets: required_dispatch_input_ordinals (compiler2/artifact.rs, graph DFS, run by the interpreter on EVERY call on two paths), local_dispatch_mask (jobs/keying.rs, matrix arms including dead arms plus every guard, run per function per root), tested_input_ordinals (dispatch_reachability.rs, all nodes, any guard means every input), and four subject-to-root recursions under them. Two of the answers can disagree today (arms after a catch-all).

The interpreter walk is 19.6% of samples on tail_recursion (interp 3.90s vs run 0.16s); the dispatch executor's per-node HashMap clone and lane-vector clones are another quarter.

Design: DispatchGraph carries input_demand: Vec<DispatchDemand>, one slot per input ordinal, accrued in DispatchGraphBuilder::add_node as each node is created. Every Test and Outcome node is reachable, only the Fail node can be orphaned and it reads nothing, so accrual at creation equals the reachable walk without the walk. required(i) is input_demand[i] != Ignore; keying reads the same vector. The builder is handed the producer's view of pins and guards; guard leaves are accrued while guard_expr_from_ast builds the expression. Pins bind at creation (the post-build loop is deleted). The guard carrier subject (input 0) is never charged.

Proof: the fold lives inside the builder and nothing at runtime can call it; the census pins plans per fixture; one telemetry event per compiled plan carries the node counts DispatchCompileStats already computes and drops. Wall clock corroborates.

Children in DAG order: .1 and .2 feed .3 (the payoff); .4 collapses the interpreter's dispatch ladder; fz-21x.27 (dense dispatch state) and .5 (lazy prepared keys) follow .4; .6 (delete DispatchCallMiss) and .7 (Rc plan facts) are independent. Defects .8 (zero-arity guard panic) and .9 (pinned bitstring size) close by construction in .3 and carry their own three-door fixture commit; .10 (pin in a head gets a construction diagnostic) is independent. Follow-ups .11 (tested flavor for reachability) and .12 (one body table) sit at the end. Related outside the epic: fz-tqd.1 (helper pins resolve in clause 0's namespace, dies with fz-21x.24) and fz-b58 (the interpreter never spends reductions).
title: [EPIC] One plan fact: a dispatch plan records what it reads of its inputs when its graph is built
